question: After final-owner denylist revocation is complete, should OpenClaw permanently support denylist policy in both `tools.exec` configuration and `exec-approvals.json`, overriding permissive full/off policy and durable trust?
rationale: The remaining code defect has a bounded repair, but code review cannot choose the permanent persisted-policy, protocol, fail-closed, and operator-impact contract.

options.title: Accept two-layer denylist
options.body: Keep both policy sources, union them, and require current-policy revocation checks at every final execution owner.

options.title: Use approvals file only
options.body: Remove `tools.exec.denylist` and keep one persisted policy owner to reduce compatibility and cross-runtime revocation complexity.

options.title: Decline deny-over-allow
options.body: Retain the existing deny, allowlist, and full modes without introducing STOP-list semantics.

recommendation.title: Accept two-layer denylist
recommendation.body: Keep both policy sources, union them, and require current-policy revocation checks at every final execution owner.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work defines the native macOS authorization owner and final delayed-approval security contract affected by this decision.
